title: How to Get Found by Recruiters on LinkedIn (And Ignore the Advice Making You Invisible)
description:
Recruiters aren't ignoring you because you lack experience. In many cases, they simply can't find you.

In this video, I'll show you how to get found by recruiters on LinkedIn and why some of the most common LinkedIn advice may actually be making your profile less visible. You'll learn how recruiters search LinkedIn, what keywords matter most, how to optimize your LinkedIn headline, About section, and work experience, and how to position yourself so recruiters immediately understand your value.

We'll cover:
 How recruiters actually use LinkedIn 
 The LinkedIn profile mistakes making you invisible
 How to optimize your LinkedIn headline for recruiter searches
 What to include in your About section
 How to write experience bullets that attract recruiters
 How to improve your LinkedIn visibility
 Networking strategies that help recruiters remember you

If you're job searching, trying to get more recruiter messages, improve your LinkedIn profile, optimize your LinkedIn headline, or increase your visibility to hiring managers and recruiters, this video is for you.

transcript: Most LinkedIn advice is completely backwards. Recruiters are not sitting on LinkedIn looking for your personal brand or your inspirational story. They are trying to fill roles quickly and they are searching for job titles, industries, systems, certifications, leadership scope, measurable results, and proof that you can solve the problem they are hiring for. If your profile is built more like social media rather than a recruiter search tool, there's a very good chance you are invisible to the people making those hiring decisions. The good news is that this problem is completely fixable. The people consistently getting recruiter messages are usually not the people with the most inspirational profiles. They are the people who are easiest to find, easiest to understand, and easiest to remember. Now, to be fair, LinkedIn absolutely can be a branding platform for creators, consultants, and business owners. However, if your primary goal is getting recruited for jobs, searchability needs to come first. That is the shift most people miss. Recruiters are not asking themselves, "Wow, what an inspirational story." They are asking, "Can this person do the job? Have they worked at the right scale? And do they match what I am searching for?" That is the reality of recruiting and one of the biggest mistakes people make on LinkedIn is quietly destroying their own visibility without even realizing it. The first thing you need to understand is that recruiters search LinkedIn using keywords. They search industries, job titles, certifications, systems, software, methodology, leadership scope, and specialties. If your profile is vague, overly creative, or packed with generic corporate fluff, you are making yourself harder to find. For example, look at these two headlines. The first says, "Rockstar healthcare leader committed to innovation and helping organizations succeed. Fun, but nobody is actually searching for that. Now, compare it to this. Enterprise healthcare strategy and business development leader directed $2 million plus growth and transformation initiative, M&A service line strategy and post-merger integration. Immediately, recruiters understand the industry, leadership level, specialization, business functions, enterprise scale, and measurable impact. Those are searchable terms tied to real hiring decisions. This is why your headline matters so much more than most people realize. Your headline should not simply be your current title unless it perfectly matches the role you want next because this is primary LinkedIn real estate. Your headline should quickly communicate what you do, your niche, your level, your specialization, and ideally the scope or impact of your work. Honestly, this is exactly why I created my Get Seen Guide. Most job seekers are accidentally blending into the crowd because their resume, LinkedIn profile, job search strategy is generic instead of immediately showing a recruiter where they fit and why they matter. Let's talk about your about section because this is where people either become memorable or sound exactly like everyone else on LinkedIn. Your about section is not your life story and it's not a motivational speech. It's definitely not results-driven professional with a proven track record of. We have to let that results-oriented professional phrase go. Your about section should do three things. It should clarify what you do, reinforce your positioning, and show the measurable impact. And yes, your profile should still sound human. A small glimpse of personality can absolutely make you more memorable and relatable. Maybe you are the person who codes for fun on the weekends. Maybe you are a huge reader and already volunteering to organize the office book club. Or maybe you will live for March Madness and if office pools are allowed, consider it organized for life. That kind of detail adds humanity. The problem is when personality becomes the entire strategy and recruiters still cannot quickly figure out what you actually do. One of my favorite frameworks is what you solve, how you think, and measurable outcomes. Then support it with real outcomes like cost savings, system optimization, revenue growth, inventory recovery, operational improvements, and the large-scale initiatives. That is what creates credibility. Now, let's talk about work experience because this is where a lot of people accidentally tank their profiles. Your experience section should not read like a boring HR description. Recruiters are trying to answer three questions fast. Can this person do the work? Have they done it at the right scale? And are they aligned with this role? So, instead of writing "responsible for project management and team coordination", show a scope, systems, leadership, business impact, technical skills, and measurable outcomes. For example, "Recovered 1 billion in Navy inventory through systems analysis and operational process improvements." That tells me something immediately. Or, "Saved 10 million in material by streamlining procurement workflows using Six Sigma methodologies." Again, specific, searchable, measurable, and credible. Now, here is one of the biggest LinkedIn mistake quietly hurting people's visibility. Most people use LinkedIn passively. They scroll, they lurk, they consume content, but they never actually participate professionally. Meanwhile, LinkedIn is constantly learning what industries you engage with, what topics you interact with, who you follow, and what conversations you participate in. So, if your feed is full of a random motivational junk, unrelated content, and things that have absolutely nothing to do with your field, start cleaning it up. Seriously. Follow recruiters, hiring managers, target companies, and professionals already doing the work you want to do. Then actually engage. Not great post, add perspective, add thoughts, comment like you're a professional peer. Because visibility compounds. One of my favorite strategies is building a target company list. Not 400 random locations, 15 to 20 companies you would genuinely love to work for. Then follow recruiters, hiring managers, department leads, and professionals to connect to those roles. Now your newsfeed stops feeling random, and that is the hidden power of LinkedIn. You are not trying to beg for a job, you are trying to become professionally familiar and relevant. That is a huge difference. Because when opportunities open up, people are far more likely to think of someone they recognize than someone who randomly applied 14 seconds ago. And that is visibility. And honestly, visibility is what most job seekers are actually missing right now. Not talent, not intelligence, and not potential. Visibility. Because the people getting opportunities right now are usually not the loudest people. They are the people who are easiest to find, understand, and remember. And if a recruiter cannot quickly figure out what you do, what level you operate at, what problems you solve, and where you fit, they move on fast. So, if you're tired of sending applications into a black hole, getting ignored by recruiters, or feeling invisible online. That is exactly what my get seen guide was built to fix. It walks you step-by-step through how to position your resume so recruiters immediately understand your value instead of skipping past you. I'll link it below. All right, job search besties.
